question: For the propagation of which faith was the Sattriya dance form introduced in Assam by Sankaradeva?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vaishnavism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form from Assam, India.
 
• It was **introduced by the Assamese saint Sankaradeva** in the 15th century.
 
• The dance form was created to **propagate the teachings of Vaishnavism**, a sect of Hinduism that worships Lord Vishnu.
 
• Sattriya was traditionally performed in **Sattras** (Vaishnavite monasteries) as part of religious rituals and ceremonies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vaishnavism** is one of the major traditions within Hinduism, focused on the worship of Lord Vishnu and his avatars, especially Rama and Krishna.
 
• **Sankaradeva** was a 15th-16th century saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer from Assam.
 
• The **Sattras** are institutions established by Sankaradeva and his disciples to promote the principles of Vaishnavism through various forms of art, including dance, drama, and music.
 
• Sattriya dance was recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
 
• Sankari culture, derived from the teachings of Sankaradeva, encompasses a wide range of cultural and artistic expressions, including dance, music, drama, and literature.
